correctness.rationale: The monomial-isomorphism lemma is proved from invertible squares, and in F_2 reduces the entire moduli equivalence to conjugation by S_5. Two independent exhaustive C++17 algorithms visit all 2^25 binary structure matrices, test invertibility over F_2, enumerate all orbits using respectively generator BFS and full-permutation lex minima, and compute full abstract stabilizer-group types, with identical 13-type spectra. They recover exactly 9,999,360 invertible matrices from 85,411 disjoint orbits; a third direct orbital-matrix Burnside calculation yields the independent conjugacy-class fixed-unit table (9,999,360; 21,504; 1,536; 504; 24; 32; 15) and the same 85,411 total. These are finite exhaustive calculations for n=5, not unproved infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Dimension five is the first case beyond the published explicit dimension-2/3/4 finite-field class-count formulas, and F_2 is the smallest field. The complete abstract automorphism-group profile of a natural first-unresolved finite moduli problem distinguishes 13 group types, including nonisomorphic groups of the same order, and yields the exact 81,408 rigid classes and 4,003 nonrigid classes. This precise finite structural invariant is not implied by the aggregate class count or rare-symmetry asymptotics and supplies a reproducible benchmark for higher-dimensional symmetry classifications. No general theorem or broad impact is claimed.
